title_en: A telling hole in a Neandertal bone hints at a bitter end
title_zh: 尼安德特人骨头上的一个洞暗示了一个痛苦的结局

paragraphs.en: The size and structure of a puncture wound in a shoulder blade suggest that it was made by a wooden spear shortly before or after death, researchers write October 15 in Scientific Reports . But violence isn’t all this Neandertal may have known. A shattered tooth found with the remains hints that the deceased suffered a facial injury at some point in their life. Surviving this injury indicates that Neandertals may have helped each other in times of need, the study authors speculate.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员在10月15日的《科学报告》上撰文指出，一块肩胛骨上穿刺伤口的尺寸和结构表明，它是在死亡前不久或死后不久被木矛刺出的。但暴力并非这具尼安德特人遗骸所经历的全部。与遗骸一同发现的一颗碎裂牙齿暗示，死者在生前的某个时刻曾遭受面部损伤。研究作者推测，能够在这类损伤中存活下来，说明尼安德特人可能在需要时互相帮助。

paragraphs.en: These remains with visible trauma are “super cool,” because “there’s a lot of ways to die that leave absolutely no mark on your skeleton,” says Libby Cowgill, a biological anthropologist at the University of Missouri in Columbia who wasn’t involved with the study.
paragraphs.zh: 密苏里大学哥伦比亚分校的生物人类学家利比·考吉尔（Libby Cowgill）没有参与这项研究。她说，这些带有明显外伤痕迹的遗骸“非常酷”，因为“有很多种死法根本不会在骨骼上留下任何痕迹”。

paragraphs.en: Neandertals were often injured throughout their lives, probably from hunting. But archaeologists have also uncovered occasional signs that Neandertals and other hominids — modern humans and their extinct cousins — were stabbing and pummeling each other, maybe even intentionally, as far back as 430,000 years ago . Signs of injuries caused by other hominids have included another Neandertal at the same Iraq site whose rib was probably stabbed .
paragraphs.zh: 尼安德特人一生中经常受伤，可能是在狩猎过程中造成的。但考古学家也偶尔发现一些迹象，表明尼安德特人和其他人科动物——现代人及其已灭绝的近亲——早在43万年前就曾互相刺伤和殴打，甚至可能是故意的。其他人科动物造成伤害的迹象包括：在同一处伊拉克遗址发现的另一具尼安德特人遗骸，其肋骨很可能被刺伤。

paragraphs.en: During an excavation that began in 2019 at Shanidar, the famous Neandertal burial site in Iraqi Kurdistan, researchers uncovered remains from at least three previously unknown individuals. The set included ribs, hand bones, teeth and a perforated shoulder bone that probably belonged to a single individual who lived around 75,000 years ago.
paragraphs.zh: 2019年，研究人员开始在伊拉克库尔德斯坦著名的尼安德特人墓葬遗址沙尼达尔（Shanidar）进行发掘，发现了至少三具此前未知的个体遗骸。这批遗骸包括肋骨、手骨、牙齿和一块带孔的肩胛骨，很可能属于同一个体，此人生活在约7.5万年前。

paragraphs.en: At first, the team had no idea what caused the hole, says Emma Pomeroy, a biological anthropologist at the University of Cambridge. “It’s so round, it’s like, what is it?” she recalls thinking at the time.
paragraphs.zh: 剑桥大学的生物人类学家艾玛·波默罗伊（Emma Pomeroy）说，起初团队完全不知道这个孔洞是怎么造成的。“它太圆了，让人不禁想，这是什么？”她回忆当时的想法说。

paragraphs.en: The team removed the shoulder blade with the surrounding sediment and tested for evidence that roots or insects had damaged the fossil. But that didn’t fit the nature of the damage.
paragraphs.zh: 团队将带有周围沉积物的肩胛骨整体取出，并检测是否有根系或昆虫破坏化石的证据。但结果与损伤的性质不符。

paragraphs.en: Instead, they found fragments of bone from the shoulder blade in the dirt that suggested it had been pierced when the individual, which the team named Shanidar A, was alive. The team also didn’t see any signs of healing around the puncture wound when they analyzed the bone under the microscope and using X-rays — suggesting that the injury had occurred around the time of death.
paragraphs.zh: 相反，他们在泥土中发现了肩胛骨的骨碎片，这表明该个体——团队将其命名为沙尼达尔A（Shanidar A）——在世时肩胛骨被刺穿。团队在显微镜下并用X射线分析骨骼时，也没有在穿刺伤口周围看到任何愈合迹象——这表明损伤发生在死亡前后。

paragraphs.en: The next task was to find out what instrument might have caused the injury. The team compared the puncture with the fossilized remains of butchered animals found alongside human tools, as well as wounds created by archaeologists stabbing animal corpses with re-created Paleolithic weapons . Stone-tipped spears usually create a diamond-shaped hole. Wooden spears, on the other hand, tend to leave round puncture wounds.
paragraphs.zh: 接下来的任务是找出可能造成损伤的工具。团队将这一穿刺伤口与人类工具旁发现的、带有屠宰痕迹的动物化石遗骸进行了比较，也与考古学家用复原的旧石器时代武器刺戳动物尸体所造成的伤口进行了比较。石尖矛通常造成菱形孔洞，而木矛则往往留下圆形穿刺伤。

paragraphs.en: The team also found a broken incisor alongside the rest of the remains. The tooth was so shattered that Shanidar A probably experienced a serious injury to their face. Tartar buildup suggests that the tooth splintered in half years before Shanidar A died, meaning they lived with their disability for a long time.
paragraphs.zh: 团队还在其他遗骸旁发现了一颗断裂的门牙。这颗牙齿碎裂严重，说明沙尼达尔A的面部可能遭受过严重损伤。牙结石的堆积表明，这颗牙齿在沙尼达尔A去世前数年就已裂成两半，这意味着他们带着这一伤残生活了很长时间。
